question: Should Oracle support a durable metadata-only command that registers externally started ChatGPT conversations as completed local sessions?
rationale: This adds a permanent CLI and persisted-session contract rather than repairing an established behavior, so implementation correctness alone cannot establish whether the workflow belongs in Oracle.

options.title: Accept after safety and proof
options.body: Keep the command after preventing deletion of non-imported sessions, removing the changelog edit, and supplying a redacted real import-and-follow-up run.

options.title: Prefer direct URL follow-up
options.body: Avoid synthetic completed sessions and instead design an explicitly supported URL-based follow-up path with clear persistence semantics.

options.title: Decline the import surface
options.body: Keep browser follow-up limited to conversations originally created and verified by Oracle.

recommendation.title: Accept after safety and proof
recommendation.body: Keep the command after preventing deletion of non-imported sessions, removing the changelog edit, and supplying a redacted real import-and-follow-up run.

likelyOwner.reason: His history spans the browser follow-up behavior, CLI routing, and repository-level product integration affected by this decision.
